speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, how long have you had these skin lesions, and have you noticed any fever or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: That exposure to chickenpox is concerning, but the lesions being painless and nonpruritic makes a typical viral exanthem less likely. Can you describe the appearance of the papules—do they look like flat spots, raised bumps, or do they have a central scab? Also, have you noticed any scaling or crusting on the lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum

REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up dermoscopy of the pearly papules with central umbilication.

The description of "pearly papules with central umbilication" is classic for Molluscum Contagiosum, which often spreads in daycare settings. Seeing these images will help confirm the diagnosis before we discuss treatment options.
